newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Democracy organisations have called on all concerned to stop mobilising and provoking people to oppose the draft charter by citing the Monarchy, saying that doing so would only "lead to conflict and confrontation similar to the May 1992 bloodshed." Students' Federation of Thailand secretary-general Suriyan Thongnu-iad says democracy organisations have resolved at a meeting to call for all concerned not to solicit public opposition to the draft charter in a provocative manner. (BANGKOK POST)

- The courts are ready to process any urgent request from police to consider closing down a print publication or television or radio programme which publishes false reports, says criminal court chief. Seeking court orders for the closure of media outlets deemed irresponsible was proposed and agreed to last week by the media monitoring committee set up and chaired by Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung. (THE NATION)

- The Chart Pattana Party has taken another apparent step in its attempt to remove Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan by demanding a say in the reshuffling of the Finance and other five economic ministries. Chart Pattana deputy leader and Industry Minister Korn Dabaransi, who makes the demand, says he will meet Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh today or tomorrow. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has called a meeting of key individuals and groups concerned with the construction of the Yadana gas pipeline project in an effort to move the project forward to completion by the deadline and to resolve all outstanding issues. The meeting is scheduled for Wednesday and will be chaired by the prime minister. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Flying in more tourists is the quickest way to counter falling occupancy rates and revenue for Thailand's hotels, say hotel owners. They say the aviation industry should be liberalised to allow more airlines to enter the country, and marketing of attractions should be stepped up. (BANGKOK POST)
